halt_summary: Driver design and probe binaries are correct (kernel barrier via POSIX_SPAWN_START_SUSPENDED, no cooperative delay, recursive kqueue+reconcile). However, the substrate this ACT was executed on blocks same-UID signal delivery from parent to its own children (EPERM on kill(child, SIGCONT) and even kill(child, SIGTERM)). This is the same EPERM boundary the predecessor ACT documented in 10-mechanism-a-recon.txt and the production helper exists to bridge. The corrected ACT's §Method requires kill(root, SIGCONT); §Driver identity disclaims kill(2) capability. These are contradictory on this substrate. The experiment did not run. Round-3 closes the lossless-reader / EOF-semantics / write-failure-visibility gaps via a verified fragmentation witness. Round-4 makes the fixture exit status the authoritative cross-process-boundary oracle-failure signal (_exit(86) + driver waitpid + SIGPIPE suppression), verified by 41-oracle-broken-channel-witness on the real fixture binary. Round-6 supersedes round-5: the round-5 two-pipe topology + reader thread was retracted because the expected set (GROUND_TRUTH_CREATED) was derived from a descendant-report pipe that was itself a source of loss -- a dropped report meant the expected set was missing that pid, so the driver could not detect the omission. Round-6 simplifies to a SINGLE GT pipe: every fixture-created process (root and every descendant) writes its CREATE record directly to GT via env.CLINEMM_GROUND_TRUTH_FD. Records are 75-100 bytes (well below PIPE_BUF=65536), so each write() is atomic on POSIX pipe(2). On a broken GT pipe, _exit(86) fires (round-4 failsafe preserved). Multithreaded-fork hazard is removed (no reader thread in root). Verified by 42-oracle-descendant-failure-witness and 43-oracle-composition-witness on the real fixture binary. Round-7 closes HALT_ORACLE_MISS_CLASSIFIER_NOT_EXERCISED: the reviewer observed that 43-witness verified MULTILEVEL_GT_RECORD_DELIVERY but did not exercise the load-bearing MISS = GT - KQUEUE_TRACKED discriminator. The pure miss classifier (tracked_has + compute_missed) was extracted into tools/macos-host-helper/native/containment-probe/miss-classifier.h as a static inline miss_classify(). Both 30- and the new 44-witness compile against the SAME production code path (no algorithm fork). 44-witness has 5 cases including the exact root->child->grandchild scenario the reviewer asked for: GT={100,101,102}, pid_start={(100,1000),(101,1100)}, TRACKED={100,101} -> missed=1, missed[0]=(pid=102,start_us=1200), driver disposition exit 5 (REFUTE). PIPE_BUF documentary correction: the portable load-bearing fact is just record_size <= PIPE_BUF (POSIX guarantees atomicity at that boundary); we no longer pin a specific PIPE_BUF value but the 44-witness asserts the C_RECORD_MAX_BYTES (64) does not exceed KNOWN_MIN_PIPE_BUF (4096). Round-8 closes HALT_DISPOSITION_WITNESS_CONTRADICTS_CLAIM: the reviewer observed that 44-witness's printed line 'driver_disposition_for_run_above: exit=0 (PASS)' directly contradicted the load-bearing claim 'exit=5 (REFUTE / MISS)'. The bug was that the witness conflated the test-failure count with the missed_count. The bounded correction: extract the production disposition function into miss-classifier.h as a static inline oracle_disposition(missed_count, write_failures, reader_fault, evidence_fail). Both 30- (main() tail) and the witnesses (44-, 45-) compile against the SAME function. The precedence is preserved verbatim: evidence_fail>reader_fault>write_failures>miss. The 44-witness's broken disposition line was removed; in its place, five new oracle_disposition() checks feed real oracle counters into the production function. A new 45-oracle-disposition-witness (114 lines) exercises the composition: classifier->disposition on the exact T5 scenario, and pins all five exit codes. Verified on agent substrate: 45-witness T5 -> miss_classify(...) -> missed_count=1, missed[0]=(pid=102,start_us=1200); oracle_disposition(mc=1,wf=0,rf=0,ef=0) -> exit=5. All five branches pinned: 0->0, miss->5, write_fail->6, reader_fault->7, evidence_fail->8. Verified on agent substrate.

round3_fixes: ORACLE_READER_LOSSLESS: drain_ground_truth() now retains incomplete records across reads (only resets when scan>=carry_len). Verified by 40-oracle-lossless-witness fragmentation test: 7 records written with split-half-and-sleep-each-side, all 7 captured.

ORACLE_EOF_SEMANTICS: driver closes its own gt_write_fd IMMEDIATELY after posix_spawn() succeeds. Per Apple pipe(2), EOF appears only when ALL write descriptors are closed. Now when the last fixture writer exits, the reader actually sees EOF.
ORACLE_NO_FINAL_DRAIN_DROP: the 'best-effort final drain' that called read() without parsing is REMOVED. Every byte read is fed through the same parser.
ORACLE_OVERFLOW_HALT: carry_len >= sizeof(buf) latches gt_reader_fault and emits a halt event. Exit code 7 reserved for this case.

ORACLE_WRITE_FAIL_VISIBLE: fixture gt_announce() retries on EAGAIN/EINTR (3 attempts, 1ms backoff), then emits a WRITE_FAILED line on the same pipe AND a stderr line. Driver counts WRITE_FAILED into gt_write_failures, emits ground_truth_write_failures in end event. Exit code 6 reserved.

round4_fixes: ORACLE_WRITE_FAILURE_FAILSAFE: gt_announce_failure() now _exit(86)s immediately on any unrecoverable write failure (EPIPE/EIO/ENXIO/EBADF/persistent EAGAIN). Exit status 86 is kernel-mediated and observable via waitpid() in the driver regardless of pipe state. The in-pipe WRITE_FAILED line is now best-effort, not load-bearing.

SIGPIPE_SUPPRESSED: Both fixture binaries (31-helper-preattach-root.c, 32-helper-preattach-emulator.c) install signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN) at process start. Without this, the kernel's default SIGPIPE action terminates the fixture before the round-4 _exit(86) failsafe can run.

DRIVER_WAITPID_ROOT_STATUS: After drain_ground_truth(), driver calls waitpid(root) with a brief grace period (SIGTERM if needed, SIGKILL last resort). If root exits with status 86, gt_oracle_evidence_fail latches; exit code 8 reserved.

SIGNAL_EXIT_NOT_LATCHED: signal-induced root exit (e.g., signal-triggered-fork SIGTERM mode) is the contract for that fixture and is NOT latched as oracle failure. Verified by signal-triggered-fork SIGTERM smoke test: root exit -15, driver does not latch.

round5_fixes_RETRACTED: TWO_PIPE_TOPOLOGY + ROOT_READER_THREAD: retracted by round-6 review. The expected set (GROUND_TRUTH_CREATED) was derived from a descendant-report pipe that was itself a source of loss -- if a descendant's report write failed, the report was missing from the expected set, so the driver could not detect the omission (textbook false-GREEN). See round6_fixes for the bounded correction.
round6_fixes: SINGLE_PIPE_TOPOLOGY: removed the descendant-report pipe and the root reader thread. EVERY fixture-created process (root + every descendant) writes its CREATE record DIRECTLY to the single GT pipe that the driver drains. env: CLINEMM_GROUND_TRUTH_FD=<gt_write_fd> only.

EXPECTED_SET_FROM_GT: GROUND_TRUTH_CREATED is now the AUTHORITATIVE expected set, derived from the SAME pipe the driver reads. A pid is either in GROUND_TRUTH_CREATED (driver saw the CREATE) or it is not (driver did not). No intermediate report->CREATE translation stage that can erase the expected set.

ATOMIC_WRITES: each CREATE record is 75-100 bytes, well below PIPE_BUF=65536 bytes. POSIX pipe(2) guarantees atomic writes for any payload <= PIPE_BUF, so concurrent writers from different processes serialize at the kernel without interleaving. No mutex or thread needed.

ROUND-4_FAILSAFE_PRESERVED: on broken GT pipe (EPIPE/EIO/ENXIO/EBADF), gt_announce_failure _exit(86)s immediately. The driver waitpid(root) observes status 86 and latches gt_oracle_evidence_fail (exit code 8).

MULTITHREADED_FORK_HAZARD_REMOVED: no pthread in root. Apple pthread_atfork docs warn that fork() in a multithreaded process is heavily restricted -- the child side can only call async-signal-safe functions. The round-6 fix avoids this entirely by eliminating the reader thread.

32_EMULATOR_UNCHANGED: 32-helper-preattach-emulator.c was not modified. Its descendants stay in C and never exec, so multiple writers to GT are safe (no fork+exec, no per-process exec-fork work that needs an inherited env var).
